hook.speaker: Bhartrihari
hook.sanskrit: निन्दन्तु नीतिनिपुणा यदि वा स्तुवन्तु लक्ष्मीः समाविशतु गच्छतु वा यथेष्टम् । अद्यैव वा मरणमस्तु युगान्तरे वा न्याय्यात्पथः प्रविचलन्ति पदं न धीराः ॥
hook.line: Let them praise or blame, let money come or go: the steady don't step off the right path.
hook.translation: Let the worldly-wise blame or praise; let fortune come or go as she pleases; let death come today or ages hence: the steadfast do not move a step from the path of what is right.
hook.why: Setbacks rarely last for those who keep going on the right path.

prasang.title: Nitishatakam: On steadfastness
prasang.summary: Steadfastness: the gods kept churning the ocean past jewels and poison until they found nectar; the steady do not leave the right path whatever people say. A struck ball bounces back and a cut tree grows again.
prasang.lesson: Setbacks rarely last for those who keep going on the right path.

hook.for_you: You are working with hope in your heart.
hook.first_line: You are working with hope in your heart.

alternates.speaker: Bhartrihari
alternates.setting: From 'Worship of Shiva': gratitude for a simple life.
alternates.sanskrit: यदेतत्स्वच्छन्दं विहरणमकार्पण्यमशनं सहार्यैः संवासः श्रुतमुपशमैकव्रतफलम् । मनो मन्दस्पन्दं बहिरपि चिरस्यापि विमृशन् न जाने कस्यैष परिणतिरुदारस्य तपसः ॥
alternates.line: Freedom, simple food, good company, learning that brings calm: what did I do to deserve this?
alternates.translation: This freedom to wander at will, food eaten without humiliation, living among noble people, learning whose only fruit is calm, a mind that stirs only gently even when it looks outward for long: I do not know what generous austerity this is the fruit of.
alternates.why: Gratitude for a simple life, and devotion without rivalry between forms of God.

prasang.title: Vairagyashatakam: Worship of Shiva
prasang.summary: Devotional verses longing for a quiet life by the Ganga in Shiva's presence, including a famous non-sectarian line that Shiva and Vishnu are one in essence.
prasang.lesson: Gratitude for a simple life, and devotion without rivalry between forms of God.

alternates.speaker: Vasishtha
alternates.setting: Vasishtha teaches the disheartened young Rama that effort, not fate, shapes his life.
alternates.sanskrit: प्राक्तनं चैहिकं चेति द्विविधं विद्धि पौरुषम् । प्राक्तनोऽद्यतनेनाशु पुरुषार्थेन जीयते ॥
alternates.line: Your past effort shaped today; your effort today can quickly change what the past set in motion.
alternates.translation: Know that effort is of two kinds, past and present. Past effort is quickly overcome by present effort.
alternates.why: Your past effort shaped today; today's effort shapes tomorrow. Don't grieve what was never in your hands.
alternates.misuse: You are not stuck with your past. It does not mean every hardship is your own doing.

prasang.title: Vasishtha on self-effort: fate is only your past effort
prasang.summary: Vasishtha's first teaching to Rama is a long case for self-effort. What people call fate is simply the fruit of their own past effort, and present effort can overcome it, as the stronger of two rams wins. He also says not to torment yourself over what was beyond your power, and to steer your habits gently, like raising a child.
prasang.lesson: Your past effort shaped today; today's effort shapes tomorrow. Don't grieve what was never in your hands.

verse.for_you: The praise will come and the silence will come. Your path is the one you walked through the long months. Keep walking it.
verse.try_today: Notice one moment of praise today, and one moment of silence, and let them both pass.
verse.scene_line: The gods kept churning the ocean until the nectar rose; you kept walking until the letter came.

verse.speaker: Lakshman
verse.setting: At Lake Pampa, Lakshman pulls Ram out of despair after Sita has been taken.
verse.sanskrit: उत्साहो बलवानार्य नास्त्युत्साहात् परं बलम्। सोत्साहस्य हि लोकेषु न किंचिदपि दुर्लभम्॥
verse.line: There is no strength greater than enthusiasm. For the one who has it, nothing is out of reach.
verse.translation: Noble brother, enthusiasm is powerful; there is no strength greater than enthusiasm. For the person who has it, nothing in the world is out of reach.
verse.why: Beauty can sharpen grief; a friend can remind you of your own strength.

prasang.title: Grief in springtime at Pampa
prasang.summary: At the beautiful lake of Pampa in spring, everything reminds Ram of Sita and his grief deepens. Lakshman tells him there is no strength greater than enthusiasm, and to rouse himself.
prasang.story_hook: Spring had come to the lake, and every flower made Ram's grief worse.
prasang.lesson: Beauty can sharpen grief; a friend can remind you of your own strength.

verse.for_you: You held to your hope through those eight months. Now that door is open. Keep your eyes on what is ahead.
verse.try_today: Notice one small step forward today and let it fuel your next move.
verse.scene_line: Like Lakshman beside Ram at Pampa, your steady energy can clear the path ahead.

why: No strength greater than the will to go on (Valmiki Ramayana, Kishkindha 1.121 (Gita Press))

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna sorts knowledge, action, doers, judgement, resolve and happiness by the three qualities.
verse.sanskrit: मुक्तसङ्गोऽनहंवादी धृत्युत्साहसमन्वितः । सिद्ध्यसिद्ध्योर्निर्विकारः कर्ता सात्त्विक उच्यते ॥
verse.line: Free of clinging and boasting, full of resolve and enthusiasm, unchanged by success or failure: the best kind of doer.
verse.translation: The doer who is free from attachment, does not speak of himself, is full of steadiness and enthusiasm, and unmoved by success or failure, is called sattvic.
verse.why: Choose the joy that's hard at first and sweet later.

prasang.title: Knowledge, action, doer, intellect, resolve and happiness by the three gunas
prasang.summary: Krishna describes clear, restless and dull versions of action, doer, judgement, resolve and happiness: the best joy is poison first and nectar later; the restless kind is nectar first and poison later.
prasang.lesson: Choose the joy that's hard at first and sweet later.

verse.meaning: The best kind of doer acts without clinging, without boasting, full of steady resolve and enthusiasm, and remains unchanged by success or failure. This is the sattvic way of acting.
verse.for_you: You are doing the work with steady enthusiasm. May the offer letter be the start of many days where you act with calm resolve.
verse.try_today: Notice the steadiness in your hands while you work today.
verse.scene_line: You stand at the start of your work, steady and full of zeal like Arjuna before the battle.

why: steadiness is named as what the best doer carries
unchanged by success or failure

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on who is truly a renouncer.
verse.sanskrit: श्री भगवानुवाचअनाश्रितः कर्मफलं कार्यं कर्म करोति यः । स संन्यासी च योगी च न निरग्निर्न चाक्रियः ॥
verse.line: The real renouncer does the work that's needed without leaning on its rewards, not the one who quits.
verse.translation: The Blessed Lord said: One who does the work that ought to be done, without depending on its fruit, is the renouncer and the yogi; not the one who gives up the sacred fire or gives up action.
verse.why: Quitting isn't renouncing; working without clinging is.

prasang.title: Action, and the one established in yoga
prasang.summary: The true renouncer is the one who does the work that ought to be done without depending on its fruit, not the one who simply stops.
prasang.lesson: Quitting isn't renouncing; working without clinging is.

verse.for_you: You have the offer in hand, and now you are free to do the work itself. The turning is here, and the work is the thing.
verse.try_today: Work on the offer today without checking for the reward.

why: quitting is not the mark of freedom; doing what is needed without leaning on the reward is
staying with the work that ought to be done
plan_v3.writer_note: Letting-go teaching for a reader who is building something. Explain it through their own situation and feeling: what is released is the grip that hurts them, never their love, their hope or their work. Never say or imply 'stop caring' or 'your hope is the problem'. Read it after the guard verse, which reassures first.

guard.line: Free of clinging and boasting, full of resolve and enthusiasm, unchanged by success or failure: the best kind of doer.

verse.speaker: Teacher
verse.setting: The graduation address as a student leaves to start family life.
verse.sanskrit: वेदमनूच्याचार्योन्तेवासिनमनुशास्ति । सत्यं वद । धर्मं चर । स्वाध्यायान्मा प्रमदः ।
verse.line: Speak the truth. Do what is right. Never stop learning.
verse.translation: Having taught the Veda, the teacher instructs the student: Speak the truth. Practise what is right. Do not neglect your study.
verse.why: Truth, right action, gratitude and graceful giving: a whole life in one speech.

prasang.title: The graduation address
prasang.summary: As a student finishes his studies and leaves to start family life, the teacher gives him parting instructions: speak truth, do right, keep learning, honour mother, father, teacher and guest, give with grace. He even tells the student to copy only the teachers' good conduct, and when in doubt to act as thoughtful, gentle people would.
prasang.lesson: Truth, right action, gratitude and graceful giving: a whole life in one speech.

verse.for_you: The door has opened, and the path ahead is yours to walk. Speak with a clear voice, do what is right, and let your learning grow as you go. This is your way forward.
verse.try_today: Notice one small way to speak truth, act rightly, or study today.
verse.scene_line: You stand at the threshold of your own life, ready to speak, to act, and to keep learning.

why: study is to be kept up, not finished
three plain commitments to carry into working life

verse.speaker: Bhartrihari
verse.setting: Closing verse of the section praising learning: the 'sword's-edge vow' of the good.
verse.sanskrit: असन्तो नाभ्यर्थ्याः सुहृदपि न याच्यः कृशधनः प्रिया न्याय्या वृत्तिर्मलिनमसुभङ्गेऽप्यसुकरम् । विपद्युच्चैः स्थेयं पदमनुविधेयं च महतां सतां केनोद्दिष्टं विषममसिधाराव्रतमिदम् ॥
verse.line: Don't beg favours from the wicked or money from a struggling friend. Stand tall in hard times.
verse.translation: Do not ask the wicked for favours; do not ask a friend of slender means for money; love a just way of earning; do nothing base even when life is at stake; stand tall in trouble; follow in the footsteps of the great. Who taught the good this vow, hard as walking a sword's edge?
verse.why: What you learn and how you speak are the wealth no one can take from you.
verse.misuse: 'Even when life is at stake' is the poet's intensity; no principle asks you to harm yourself.

prasang.title: Nitishatakam: In praise of learning and the learned
prasang.summary: Bhartrihari praises learning as wealth no thief can take and speech as the one lasting ornament, then turns to good company and the three kinds of people who face obstacles. It ends with the 'sword's-edge vow' of the good.
prasang.lesson: What you learn and how you speak are the wealth no one can take from you.

verse.for_you: You have walked through eight months of seeking and now the door is open. Keep your feet on the path of what you know is fair.
verse.try_today: Notice one choice today that is clean and upright.
verse.scene_line: You stand at your new desk, the offer letter in your hand, choosing a just way forward.

why: The sword-edge vow of integrity

story.title: Nitishatakam: In praise of learning and the learned
story.summary: Bhartrihari praises learning as wealth no thief can take and speech as the one lasting ornament, then turns to good company and the three kinds of people who face obstacles. It ends with the 'sword's-edge vow' of the good.
story.lesson: What you learn and how you speak are the wealth no one can take from you.
story.teaser: Nitishatakam: In praise of learning and the learned
story.for_you: You kept going through the long wait. That resolve is already yours. Hold it gently as you move forward.

why: The lowly do not start for fear of obstacles; the middling stop when obstacles come; the best never give up what they have begun.

verse.speaker: Kausalya
verse.setting: Holding back tears, Kausalya blesses her son before he leaves for fourteen years in the forest.
verse.sanskrit: यं पालयसि धर्म त्वं प्रीत्या च नियमेन च। स वै राघवशार्दूल धर्मस्त्वामभिरक्षतु॥
verse.line: May the good you have lived by, gladly and faithfully, now protect you.
verse.translation: May the goodness you have kept so gladly and so faithfully protect you, tiger of the Raghus.
verse.misuse: A mother's blessing, not a promise that good people never suffer.
verse.for_you: The discipline you have kept so gladly now turns to guard you. Let this good keep its hold. It is your protection now.
verse.try_today: Notice one small act today that shows your discipline at work.
verse.scene_line: You stand at the start of a long road, and the goodness you have lived by stands with you.

why: trust that a life of right conduct protects
a mother's blessing to carry into hardship

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Arjuna asks about faith outside the rules; Krishna explains faith follows nature.
verse.sanskrit: सत्त्वानुरूपा सर्वस्य श्रद्धा भवति भारत । श्रद्धामयोऽयं पुरुषो यो यच्छ्रद्धः स एव सः ॥
verse.line: You are made of what you deeply believe. As your faith is, so are you.
verse.translation: Everyone's faith follows their nature, Bharata. A person is made of faith; as a person's faith is, so is that person.
verse.why: You become what you deeply believe.

prasang.title: Faith, and harsh austerity against scripture
prasang.summary: Everyone's faith matches their nature; a person is made of their faith. Harsh self-torment against scripture is condemned.
prasang.lesson: You become what you deeply believe.

verse.for_you: You are made of what you deeply believe, and your offer letter shows the faith you have put into this search. What you trusted in is now becoming what you are.
verse.try_today: Notice what you hold in your mind today, and let that guide your next step.
verse.scene_line: Arjuna, you stand before Krishna, and your faith in this path has already shaped who you are.

why: You become what you hold in mind (Bhagavad Gita 8.6)

verse.speaker: A brahmin (retold by Bhishma)
verse.setting: The brahmin tells the grieving King Senajit how to meet whatever life brings.
verse.sanskrit: सुखं वा यदि वा दुःखं प्रियं वा यदि वाऽप्रियम् / प्राप्तं प्राप्तमुपासीत हृदयेनापराजितः
verse.line: Pleasant or painful, meet whatever comes with a heart that refuses to be defeated.
verse.translation: Whether it is happiness or sorrow, something pleasant or unpleasant, meet whatever comes with a heart that is not defeated.
verse.why: No one suffers forever. Meet what comes with an undefeated heart.

matched.label: Everything in my life is changing at once

prasang.title: King Senajit and the brahmin's consolation
prasang.summary: King Senajit is crushed by his son's death. A brahmin comforts him: everyone suffers, no sorrow lasts forever, effort beats idleness, and whatever we call 'mine' becomes a source of pain.
prasang.lesson: No one suffers forever. Meet what comes with an undefeated heart.

verse.for_you: You have found your footing after months of waiting. Keep that steady heart as you step into this new chapter.
verse.try_today: Notice one moment today when you feel fully present, and let it stand as proof your heart is not defeated.
verse.scene_line: You stand in your new office, ready to meet the next thing that arrives.

why: Whatever arrives can be met
Aparajita hridaya, the undefeated heart, is the quality named

verse.speaker: Shiva
verse.setting: Shiva explains to his devotee Bhringi what makes a 'great enjoyer'.
verse.sanskrit: महान्ति सुखदुःखानि यः पयांसीव सागरः । समं समुपगृह्णाति महाभोक्ता स उच्यते ॥
verse.line: Take in big joys and big sorrows the way the ocean takes in rivers: evenly.
verse.translation: One who takes in great joys and sorrows evenly, as the ocean takes in the waters of rivers: that one is called a great enjoyer.
verse.why: Work fully, enjoy fully, let go fully; anchored inside, you can do it all without burning out.

matched.label: Everything in my life is changing at once

prasang.title: Shiva's three vows: be a great doer, enjoyer and letter-go
prasang.summary: Vasishtha gives Rama three vows that Shiva once gave his devotee Bhringi: be a great doer, a great enjoyer, and a great renouncer. A great doer acts fully and on time without clinging; a great enjoyer takes in joys and sorrows evenly, like the ocean takes in rivers; a great renouncer lets go inside. Live this way and work won't wear you out.
prasang.lesson: Work fully, enjoy fully, let go fully; anchored inside, you can do it all without burning out.

verse.try_today: Notice one moment of joy today without trying to make it last forever.
verse.scene_line: You stand in a new office, watching the waters of change enter you like the ocean.

why: room enough for whatever arrives
joy and sorrow taken in alike

verse.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
verse.setting: Lecture 'Work and Its Secret', Los Angeles, 4 January 1900.
verse.line: pay as much attention to the means of work as to its end.
verse.translation: One of the greatest lessons I have learnt in my life is to pay as much attention to the means of work as to its end. … With the means all right, the end must come.
verse.why: Look after the means; keep the power to let go.

prasang.title: Work and its secret (Los Angeles, 1900)
prasang.summary: His greatest lesson, he says, was to attend to the means as much as the end. Most failures come from neglecting the means, and most sorrow from clinging to what is already failing. Weakness invites misery, yet a heart that refuses to love also loses life's joys.
prasang.lesson: Look after the means; keep the power to let go.

verse.for_you: You have the offer. Now let your care for each small step be as steady as your care for the goal itself.
verse.try_today: Notice one small detail of your work today and give it your full care.

why: care over each step
the means are the part that is ours

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna's final counsel: act with devotion, reflect, choose, and take refuge.
verse.sanskrit: इति ते ज्ञानमाख्यातं गुह्याद्गुह्यतरं मया । विमृश्यैतदशेषेण यथेच्छसि तथा कुरु ॥
verse.line: I've told you all I know. Reflect on it fully, then do as you choose.
verse.translation: Thus I have declared to you this knowledge, more secret than all secrets. Reflect on it fully, and then do as you wish.
verse.why: Reflect fully, choose freely, and set down the fear.

prasang.title: Action with devotion: surrender
prasang.summary: Krishna urges Arjuna to offer all action, warns that ego will only trip him, tells him to reflect fully and then choose, and finally to take refuge in him alone and not grieve.
prasang.lesson: Reflect fully, choose freely, and set down the fear.

verse.for_you: You have this knowledge now, the most hidden of all. You are ready to reflect and act. Let your choice be your own.
verse.try_today: Before you act today, pause and reflect fully on your choice.
verse.scene_line: You stand at the start of a new path, and Krishna asks you to reflect fully and then choose.

why: full reflection before acting is the instruction
Reflect fully, then decide and begin.

story.title: Angad in Ravana's court
story.story_hook: Angad sat down in the enemy's court, and they began to insult his father.
story.summary: Ram sends Angad as envoy, asking him to speak so the work gets done and it does Ravana good too. In court Ravana insults Angad, his dead father and his lord. Angad bears it, remembering that a lion gains no glory by killing a jackal. At last he plants his foot and dares anyone to move it; no warrior can.
story.lesson: Under insult, keep your purpose; a steady mind does not leave what is right.
story.hook_title: Young Angad sat in Ravana's court while they insulted his dead father
story.teaser: Young Angad sat in Ravana's court while they insulted his dead father
story.for_you: You have a brief to deliver and a foot to plant. Let the noise of the last eight months fall. Keep your footing on the offer in front of you.

why: In a hostile negotiation, stay on the brief; let insults fall and do not let them move your foot.

Should I quit my job or stay
My manager took credit for my work
I can't stay consistent
I keep procrastinating
I'm addicted to my phone

queries.hook: A fire lit by seeing what others achieved; the resolve to rise, gather your strength and take on what is yours to do.
queries.diagnose: Doubt and delay feed each other; waiting to feel ready keeps us stuck, and the unacted-on decision weighs more than the work.
queries.steady: No effort on the right path is ever wasted; even a little of it protects you and carries you forward.
queries.act: Rise and do the next right thing; act without waiting for certainty, and keep at it day by day.
queries.story: A story of someone who set out to build or win something that was theirs to do, met the first test, and kept going.

understanding.life_context: Working. Feels determined; closest to in my life is changing at once" and I quit my job or stay".

verse.speaker: Savitri
verse.setting: Knowing her husband will die in three days, Savitri takes a hard three-night vow; her father-in-law worries.
verse.sanskrit: न कार्यस्तात संतापः पारयिष्याम्यहं व्रतम् / व्यसंसायकृतं हीदं व्यवसायश्च कारणम्
verse.line: I started this with determination, and determination will carry me to the end.
verse.translation: Don't be distressed, father. I will see this vow through. It was begun with determination, and determination is what carries it to the end.
verse.why: Steady love and clear speech can face even death. Determination carries what fear would drop.

prasang.title: Savitri and Satyavan
prasang.summary: Princess Savitri marries Satyavan knowing he will die within a year. On the fated day she follows Yama, the lord of death, speaking such wisdom about goodness and friendship that he grants boon after boon, until she wins back her husband's life.
prasang.story_hook: Savitri knew the exact day her husband would die, and she went into the forest with him anyway.
prasang.lesson: Steady love and clear speech can face even death. Determination carries what fear would drop.

verse.for_you: You started with resolve eight months ago, and that same resolve is bringing you to the end. This offer letter is the proof that determination carries the work to completion. Let your determination keep moving you forward today.
verse.try_today: Notice the resolve that set this in motion today.
verse.scene_line: You stand beside Savitri, who holds her vow with the same steady mind.

why: Savitri speaks from inside a decision already made
Determination is named as the cause that carries the work

verse.speaker: Shandilya
verse.sanskrit: सर्वं खल्विदं ब्रह्म तज्जलानिति शान्त उपासीत । अथ खलु क्रतुमयः पुरुषो यथाक्रतुरस्मिꣳल्लोके पुरुषो भवति तथेतः प्रेत्य भवति स क्रतुं कुर्वीत ॥
verse.line: A person is made of resolve. As you resolve in this life, so you become. So resolve well.
verse.translation: All this is Brahman; from it all arises, into it all dissolves, in it all breathes; so one should meditate on it calmly. A person is made of resolve. As one's resolve is in this world, so one becomes on departing. So let one form a resolve.
verse.for_you: The offer letter is a sign of your resolve taking shape. Keep holding to what you are becoming.
verse.try_today: Notice what you hold to when you feel your energy rising.

why: A person is made of resolve (Chandogya Upanishad 3.14.1)

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on the inner happiness of one who sees clearly.
verse.sanskrit: न प्रहृष्येत्प्रियं प्राप्य नोद्विजेत्प्राप्य चाप्रियम् । स्थिरबुद्धिरसम्मूढो ब्रह्मविद्ब्रह्मणि स्थितः ॥
verse.line: Don't get carried away by good news or crushed by bad. Keep your understanding steady.
verse.translation: One should not rejoice on getting what is pleasant nor be troubled on getting what is unpleasant. Steady in understanding and undeluded, the knower of Brahman abides in Brahman.
verse.why: Pleasures that start and end can't hold your happiness; find the joy within.

prasang.title: The yoga of knowledge
prasang.summary: Krishna describes the wise: equal-eyed towards all beings, not elated or crushed, finding joy within, seeing that sense pleasures end in sorrow, and able to withstand desire and anger.
prasang.lesson: Pleasures that start and end can't hold your happiness; find the joy within.

verse.for_you: You have found your footing again after eight months. Let this good news be a sign of what is possible. Keep it steady.
verse.scene_line: You stand with the offer letter in your hand while the knower of Brahman remains steady and undeluded beside you.

why: a steady understanding
neither carried away nor crushed

verse.speaker: Vidula
verse.setting: Queen Vidula rouses her son Sanjaya, who lies defeated and despairing after losing his kingdom.
verse.sanskrit: सर्वेषां कर्मणां तात फले नित्यमनित्यता / अनित्यमिति जानन्तो न भवन्ति भवन्ति च अथ ये नैव कुर्वन्ति नैव जातु भवन्ति ते / ऐकगुण्यमनीहायामभावः कर्मणां फलम्
verse.line: Every result is uncertain. Some who try succeed and some don't. Those who never try never do.
verse.translation: The result of every action is uncertain. Knowing this, some people act and succeed, some do not. But those who never act never succeed at all.
verse.why: Past failure doesn't define you. Results are uncertain, but those who never try never succeed.

prasang.title: Vidula rouses her defeated son
prasang.summary: Kunti sends Yudhishthira the old story of Queen Vidula, who finds her son lying defeated after losing his kingdom. She shames, then reasons, then encourages him until he rises and fights for it again.
prasang.story_hook: A prince lay in bed after losing everything, until his mother walked in and refused to let him stay there.
prasang.lesson: Past failure doesn't define you. Results are uncertain, but those who never try never succeed.

verse.for_you: You kept going through eight months of looking. That persistence is now meeting its own reward. Trust the path you are on and let your next step be just as steady.
verse.try_today: Notice one small thing today that proves you are still moving forward.
verse.scene_line: You stand at the threshold of a new chapter, just as Sanjaya rose to fight for his kingdom again.

why: Uncertainty is admitted and made a reason to act
Fear of failing is weighed against the certainty of not trying

verse.speaker: Vasishtha
verse.setting: Near the end of his teaching, Vasishtha gives Rama three vows to live by.
verse.sanskrit: महाकर्ता महाभोक्ता महात्यागी भवानघ । सर्वाः शङ्काः परित्यज्य धैर्यमालम्ब्य शाश्वतम् ॥
verse.line: Be a great doer, a great enjoyer, a great letter-go. Drop your doubts and hold steady.
verse.translation: Be a great doer, a great enjoyer, and a great renouncer, sinless one, casting off all doubts and holding to lasting steadiness.
verse.why: Work fully, enjoy fully, let go fully; anchored inside, you can do it all without burning out.

prasang.title: Shiva's three vows: be a great doer, enjoyer and letter-go
prasang.summary: Vasishtha gives Rama three vows that Shiva once gave his devotee Bhringi: be a great doer, a great enjoyer, and a great renouncer. A great doer acts fully and on time without clinging; a great enjoyer takes in joys and sorrows evenly, like the ocean takes in rivers; a great renouncer lets go inside. Live this way and work won't wear you out.
prasang.lesson: Work fully, enjoy fully, let go fully; anchored inside, you can do it all without burning out.

verse.for_you: You have the offer. Let this be the steadiness you hold onto. Work with full hands, take in the joy, and let the rest go.
verse.scene_line: You stand at the start of this new work, acting fully, enjoying fully, and letting go fully.

why: lasting steadiness as the base
act, enjoy and let go fully

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on the power of understanding to end confusion and guilt.
verse.sanskrit: तस्मादज्ञानसंभूतं हृत्स्थं ज्ञानासिनाऽऽत्मनः । छित्त्वैनं संशयं योगमातिष्ठोत्तिष्ठ भारत ॥
verse.line: Cut the doubt in your heart with clear understanding, then stand up and act.
verse.translation: Therefore, cutting with the sword of knowledge this doubt in your heart born of ignorance, take refuge in yoga, and stand up, Bharata.
verse.why: Learn humbly, trust the process, and cut through doubt to act.

prasang.title: The glory of knowledge
prasang.summary: Krishna praises knowledge: learn it humbly from those who know, it carries even the worst wrongdoer across, faith and self-control bring it, and doubt destroys. He ends: cut your doubt and stand up.
prasang.lesson: Learn humbly, trust the process, and cut through doubt to act.

verse.for_you: The offer is here and the ground is solid. You do not need to doubt the next step. Stand up and let the work begin.
verse.try_today: Notice the moment you stand up to begin your day, and let that be your clear action.
verse.scene_line: You stand up beside Arjuna, ready to act on clear understanding.

why: knowledge as the blade
'stand up': the chapter ends on rising

story.title: Indra and Virochana with Prajapati
story.story_hook: Two rivals, a god and a demon, arrived at Prajapati's door on the same day with the same question.
story.summary: Indra of the gods and Virochana of the demons study with Prajapati for 32 years to learn the self. Shown their dressed-up reflections, both leave satisfied; Virochana goes home teaching that the body is everything. Indra stops halfway, sees the flaw, and keeps coming back for 101 years until he learns that the self is not the body.
story.lesson: Don't settle for the first comfortable answer; keep asking until it holds.
story.hook_title: The king of the gods and a demon king asked the same teacher the same question
story.teaser: The king of the gods and a demon king asked the same teacher the same question
story.for_you: Your offer letter is the first answer that satisfies, but the work ahead asks you to keep coming back. The path is your honesty about what still does not add up.

why: The first answer that satisfies you may be the place you stop growing; honesty about what still does not add up is the path.
